newsitem.title: USA: GE unit, Thomas create procurement service.
newsitem.headline: GE unit, Thomas create procurement service.

text.p: GE Information Services and Thomas Publishing Co said Monday they created a joint venture out of existing operations at the two firms to offer a Web-based procurement service for corporate purchasing agents.
The new company, to be called TPN Register, will begin operations in April with users of the two companies' existing information services.
TPN is intended to blend GE's delivery service and Thomas's content, including supplier and price information and descriptive line-item detail under 55,000 product headings.
Specific financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.

The service will band together current users of GE's Trading Process Network and Thomas's ConnectsUs service. The partners said they expected TPN to handle $1 billion in transactions this year, and roughly $5 billion in 1998.
Current customers include GE Lighting, GE Capital and GE Aircraft Engines, 3M Co and Textron Inc's Automotive unit.
"By the end of 1998 we expect there will be about $5 billion in transactions flowing through the system," GE Information spokesman John Berry said in a phone interview.
The approach lets company purchasing agents post requests for proposals on a Web site. Suppliers would be able to submit private bids to the site and conduct structured negotiations with the buyers.
"It's all done electronically," Berry said, adding that the service is projected to reduce procurement response times by up to 50 percent, and cut procurements costs by up to 30 percent.
TNP will be based in the Washington, D.C. area. The venture will initially employ a staff of 30, the GE spokesman said.

Rockville, Md.-based GEIS is the recognized leader in electronic commerce systems used to connect manufacturing companies and their suppliers. Thomas, a leading publisher of business information directories, is based in New York City.
